news.headline: Walmart Reports Q1 FY2027 Before the Bell; Consumer Spending Tone Key for Retail Sector
news.body: Walmart released Q1 FY2027 results before the open on May 21, with consensus expecting ~$174 billion in revenue and $0.65 EPS. Investing.com data showed a modest +1.37% EPS surprise with a slight revenue beat, though the stock fell ~2.87% in reaction. Tariff pass-through commentary and comparable-store sales trends were the primary focus, as Walmart serves as a bellwether for the entire U.S. retail complex including Costco, Target, and the dollar stores. Management had previously guided Q1 constant-currency sales growth of 3.5%–4.5% and reiterated full-year EPS of $2.75–$2.85.

news.headline: Nvidia Q1 FY2027 Beats on Revenue and EPS; Stock Slips Despite Record $82B Quarter
news.body: Nvidia reported Q1 FY2027 EPS of $1.87 vs. consensus $1.76 (+6.25% beat) and revenue of $81.62 billion vs. estimates of ~$79.2 billion, with CEO Jensen Huang declaring 'demand has gone parabolic' driven by agentic AI adoption. CFO Colette Kress signaled $20 billion in CPU revenue this year as Nvidia targets becoming the 'world's leading CPU supplier.' Q2 guidance came in at $89.1–$92.8 billion, well above Street estimates. Despite the beat-and-raise, NVDA shares slipped ~4% post-close, continuing a pattern of muted post-earnings reactions as analyst expectations had already been pulled above guidance.

news.headline: Intuit Stock Drops 11.8% Despite Q3 Beat; Weak Revenue Growth Disappoints Market
news.body: Intuit reported Q1 CY2026 revenue of $8.56 billion (in line with estimates, +10.4% YoY) and adjusted EPS of $12.80 vs. consensus $12.57, a 1.8% beat. Management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $23.83 at the midpoint, a 3.2% increase, and guided Q2 revenue 3.1% above consensus. Despite the beat, INTU shares fell 11.8% as investors reacted to decelerating growth—revenue growth of 10.4% compared to a 18.7% five-year CAGR—and the stock's approximately 36% YTD decline signaling persistent investor concern over AI disruption risk to its core tax and accounting software franchise.

news.headline: GameStop Boosts eBay Stake to 6.6%, Intensifying Hostile Takeover Campaign
news.body: GameStop disclosed a regulatory filing on May 20 raising its economic stake in eBay from ~5% to 6.55%, including directly held shares and put/call options, escalating CEO Ryan Cohen's $56 billion unsolicited bid that eBay previously rejected as 'neither credible nor attractive.' Analysts at Wedbush suggest the accumulation may be a precursor to a proxy fight for board seats. eBay shares rose over 4% to a new 52-week high of $118.83, while GME gained ~2%. The situation is closely watched as eBay is approximately five times larger than GameStop by market cap.

news.headline: ServiceNow Surges ~10% on BofA Upgrade, AI Governance Thesis Rerating
news.body: ServiceNow shares rallied sharply over May 19–20, gaining over 10% cumulatively, after Bank of America analyst Tal Liani reinstated coverage with a Buy rating and a $130 price target, arguing AI is the strongest tailwind the company has ever seen rather than an existential threat. Bernstein also raised its price target to $236, framing NOW as an 'AI operating layer for enterprise.' The move followed ServiceNow's Knowledge 2026 event showcasing AI Control Tower and autonomous workflow products, and Q1 subscription revenue of $3.67 billion (+22% YoY) with remaining performance obligations rising 25% to over $27.7 billion.

news.headline: SoftBank Group surges >16% on Nvidia blowout earnings, AI portfolio gains
news.body: SoftBank Group shares rocketed more than 16% in Tokyo trading on May 21 after Nvidia reported quarterly revenue surging 85% to $81.62 billion, validating SoftBank's massive AI infrastructure bets. SoftBank's exposure runs through its controlling stake in Arm Holdings — whose chip designs power Nvidia-linked data centers — and a $30 billion-plus investment in OpenAI, which generated $45 billion in investment gains in the year ended March. Arm-related optimism and renewed speculation over a potential OpenAI listing amplified the move. The surge also lifted wider Asian AI-linked names: SK Hynix jumped over 8%, Japan's Renesas Electronics rose 7%, and Tokyo Electron gained 5.4%.

news.headline: Samsung Electronics +6% as 47,000-worker strike averted via tentative pay deal
news.body: Samsung Electronics shares surged more than 6% on May 21 after the company's largest labor union suspended a planned 18-day strike set to begin that day, reaching a tentative wage agreement with management. The walkout would have involved roughly 47,000 workers — about 40% of Samsung's South Korean workforce — and JPMorgan had estimated potential operating profit losses of $14–$20 billion. The deal removed a major tail risk to global DRAM and memory chip supply at a time of acute semiconductor shortages. The broader KOSPI surged 6%, snapping a four-day losing streak.

news.headline: Japan April exports surge 14.8%, fastest pace since January on chip shipment boom
news.body: Japan's Ministry of Finance reported April exports rose 14.8% year-on-year — sharply above the Reuters consensus of 9.3% — driven by a 41.6% surge in semiconductor shipments, marking the eighth consecutive month of export growth. Exports to China climbed 15.5% and to ASEAN 19.9%, while electrical machinery exports jumped 28.6%. The data confounded stagflation concerns and catalysed a Nikkei 225 rally of more than 3% on the day. Markets viewed the print as evidence that Japan's tech export cycle remains robust despite Middle East supply disruptions.

news.headline: KOSPI surges 6%, Kosdaq +5.5% as Samsung deal and Nvidia spark broad tech rally
news.body: South Korea's KOSPI jumped 6.00% and the small-cap Kosdaq added 5.55% on May 21, snapping a four-session losing streak that had wiped out earlier record highs above 8,000. The rally was driven by Samsung's strike suspension, SK Hynix's 8%-plus gain on Nvidia's AI chip demand outlook, and fading geopolitical risk as Trump signalled US-Iran negotiations were in their final stage. The MSCI Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index climbed 1.2%. The session reversed a brutal May 20 decline when Samsung had fallen 8.6% on strike fears and broader tech selling.

news.headline: Asia-Pacific markets sold off May 20 as bond yields surged and Samsung strike loomed
news.body: Asian equities fell broadly on May 20 as 30-year US Treasury yields briefly hit 5.197% — the highest since July 2007 — stoking inflation fears and triggering risk-off selling across the region. Samsung Electronics plunged 8.6% after its union confirmed it would proceed with the planned 18-day strike starting May 21; SK Hynix fell 7.6%. Japan's Nikkei dropped ~2% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng lost 1.6%. The sell-off was compounded by President Trump warning he was "an hour away" from ordering Iran strikes, before postponing action, keeping oil near $110/bbl Brent.

news.headline: WTI Crude Drops >5% Below $100 as Trump Says Iran Talks in 'Final Stages'
news.body: WTI crude futures fell more than 5% to close at $98.26/bbl on May 20 — the first sub-$100 close in weeks — after President Trump told reporters the U.S. is in the 'final stages' of negotiations with Iran. Brent also shed more than 5% to settle at $105.02/bbl. The move was amplified by satellite data confirming three supertankers transited the Strait of Hormuz, raising hopes of a gradual resumption of the ~20 mb/d corridor that has been largely blocked since March. Citibank and Wood Mackenzie both flagged a wide scenario range: Brent near $80/bbl if Hormuz reopens by June versus near $200/bbl if blockade persists through year-end.

news.headline: FOMC April Minutes Signal Rate-Hike Risk, Pressuring Gold Below $4,500
news.body: Minutes from the April 28–29 FOMC meeting released May 20 showed a majority of Fed officials indicated 'some policy firming would likely become appropriate' if inflation stays persistently above 2%, with four dissenters marking the most divided vote since 1992. Markets have fully priced out 2026 rate cuts and now assign ~40% odds to a December hike per CME FedWatch, pushing the 10-year Treasury yield to its highest since 2023. Gold traded around $4,470–$4,504 range on May 20, having retreated ~19% from its January all-time high of $5,586/oz as rising real yields and USD strength weigh on the non-yielding metal. Traders are closely watching the May 21 FOMC minutes release and upcoming PCE data for further rate-path signals.

news.headline: US Crude Inventories Fall for 4th Straight Week; SPR Depleted 10 Mb
news.body: EIA weekly data released May 20 showed U.S. commercial crude inventories fell for a fourth consecutive week, with the most recent report (week ended May 8) showing a 4.306 mb draw to 452.9 mb — double the expected 2.1 mb draw. The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve was drawn down by 10 million barrels, a 6.6% decline year-on-year, as the government attempts to offset Hormuz-driven supply losses. Gasoline stocks also fell by more than twice the expected drawdown. The persistent inventory tightening, even as WTI briefly broke below $100, underscores that physical crude markets remain severely strained and supports the EIA's forecast of an average 8.5 mb/d global inventory draw in Q2 2026.

news.headline: Global LNG Prices Stay Elevated as Golden Pass Train 1 Adds U.S. Export Capacity
news.body: EIA's May Short-Term Energy Outlook (released May 12, data active through May 20) confirmed global LNG prices remain elevated due to reduced Qatari and Gulf flows through the closed Strait of Hormuz, maintaining a wide spread between Henry Hub (~$3.50/MMBtu) and European/Asian import prices. In April, Golden Pass LNG exported its first cargo from Train 1, adding ~0.7 Bcf/d of U.S. export capacity — the ninth U.S. LNG terminal to become operational. Cheniere also ramped Train 5 at Corpus Christi Stage 3. The EIA expects U.S. LNG exports to keep rising through 2027 as elevated international prices create strong arbitrage incentives, partially offsetting lost Qatari volumes through Hormuz.

news.headline: Copper Falls to 2-Week Low on China Demand Miss and Iran-Driven Rate-Hike Fears
news.body: Copper futures dropped to around $6.10/lb on May 19 — a two-week low — as weak Chinese macro data (retail sales and industrial production both missed expectations, fixed asset investment contracted unexpectedly) compounded hawkish Fed repricing triggered by the Hormuz energy shock. The combined pressure of higher oil-driven inflation, rising borrowing costs, and softening Chinese industrial activity is squeezing industrial metals demand outlook. J.P. Morgan estimates that Brent sustained near $110/bbl could strip 1.4 percentage points from 2026 copper demand growth, with further downside if oil prices push higher. Copper had hit record highs above $14,500/mt in January before retreating to the $13,000/mt area by mid-April.
